source_refs.note: Exercise 13.1, Question 11 (book page 248, PDF 253); answer key PDF 310-311. Key's -2 ft/sec is wrong; correct 0 ft/sec.

blocks.prompt: 11 A stone is thrown upwards and its height after \(t\) seconds is given by: \(s(t) = -16t^2 + 32t + 10\) (in feet). Find the instantaneous velocity at \(t = 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Instantaneous velocity is \(s'(1)\).
Plan: first principles at \(t = 1\): expand \(s(1 + \delta t)\), subtract \(s(1)\), divide by \(\delta t\), take the limit; then interpret the answer.
steps:
Given: \(s(t) = -16t^2 + 32t + 10\) ft, \(t_1 = 1\) s.
To find: \(v(1) = s'(1)\).
Method: instantaneous velocity at \(t = t_1\) is the derivative \(v(t_1) = \lim_{\delta t \to 0} \frac{s(t_1 + \delta t) - s(t_1)}{\delta t}\) (Section 13.2.1), found here by first principles.

Subtract and divide by \(\delta t\)
\[s(1 + \delta t) - s(1) = -16(\delta t)^2\]
\[\dfrac{s(1 + \delta t) - s(1)}{\delta t} = -16\,\delta t\]
Why: \(\delta t \neq 0\) yet, so it cancels once.

Take the limit
\[v(1) = \lim_{\delta t \to 0}(-16\,\delta t) = 0\]
Why: Put \(\delta t = 0\).

Meaning of the answer
\[v(1) = 0,\quad s(1) = 26\ \text{ft}\]
Why: At \(t = 1\) the stone stops for an instant at its highest point, \(26\) ft, before falling back.

Check
\[s'(t) = -32t + 32\]
\[s'(1) = -32 + 32 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The general derivative at \(t = 1\) also gives \(0\).
blocks.final_answer: \(v(1) = 0\) ft/sec (the stone is at its highest point, \(26\) ft)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(-2\) ft/sec. This is wrong: \(s'(t) = -32t + 32\), so \(s'(1) = 0\) ft/sec; the stone is momentarily at rest at its highest point.
